text:
sophia: FYI customer in Sydney reports sudden 401 spikes + ~350ms added latency. Their traffic is landing in us-east-1 instead of ap-southeast-2. Started ~2h ago after a reported ISP firmware/edge update. attaching quick repro and headers I captured.

ajay: thanks — can you paste the dig/curl you ran? curious if EDNS or client IP is being rewritten by their resolver.

sophia: pasted outputs below. I redacted customer IP but included the nat'd IP the request shows.

sophia: ```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example A @8.8.8.8
3.120.45.78

;; edns-client-subnet: 203.0.113.45/32 (client reported by resolver)

$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Host: api.redwood.example" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models/list
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Pop: us-east-1
X-Request-Id: req_01EabcXYZ

{"error":"token not valid for region"}
```

ajay: that X-Redwood-Pop header is the runtime we saw allocate — confirms routing to us-east. edns-client-subnet shows the resolver advertising 203.0.113.45 which is a NAT gateway owned by customer's ISP. ISP likely strips ECS or overwrites it. If resolver reports a US/GEO ip or a NAT middlebox, our geoip mapping will point to the wrong pop.

mike: also seeing a small spike in cross-pop auth cache misses around the same time in traces: token lookup falls back to central auth and we reject because token binding is region-scoped. rolling back region-binding for tokens might be a mitigation but has security implications.

ajay: short-term mitigations: 1) Add account-level static region hint for this customer to force ap-southeast-2. 2) Ask customer to use a public resolver that preserves ECS (if possible). 3) File an incident with their ISP to stop rewriting EDNS/overriding client subnet.

sophia: attempting #1 now — can infra add a traffic override rule for account acct_0X123 to ap-southeast-2 (duration 24h)? need it to stop the 401s ASAP.

mike: I can push a temporary routing override. note: this will bypass some autoscaling affinity for the account. doing it now.

opsbot: deploy-override: routing override for acct_0X123 -> ap-southeast-2 applied by mike at 2067004355 :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: heads up — forced routing to ap-southeast-2 may increase egress/GPU cost for this account. estimated delta ~$150/day while override is active.

ajay: for long term we should: 1) detect sudden EDNS/client-IP flips and auto-fail to last-known-good region for auth; 2) add explicit guidance in support docs about ISP NAT/EDNS issues + sample diagnostics; 3) ask DNS provider for visibility/filtering of ECS anomalies.

sophia: collecting extra traces from customer (tcpdump/traceroute) and asking for their resolver hostname. customer says ISP uses "carrier-nat-isp-101". opening a vendor ticket with our DNS provider with these details.

mike: also adding an alert rule: if >2% of traffic from a single account changes resolved geo-pop within 30m, trigger ops review.

ajay: repro steps for support engineers (copy to thread):
1) run `dig +edns=0 +short api.redwood.example @<customer-resolver>` and note edns-client-subnet.
2) curl with verbose headers to capture X-Redwood-Pop and X-Request-Id.
3) if pop != expected, set temporary account region override and collect tcpdump/traceroute from customer.

sophia: thanks all — override seems to have stopped the 401s immediately per customer. leaving ticket open until ISP and DNS provider confirm root cause. I'll attach the vendor ticket ID here once created. :thumbsup:
